title: Shadow Work: The Distinction Detector
opening: A strong reaction can raise a question about what you value. Separate what happened from the quality you assigned, then look for examples and counterexamples before you draw an inference.

labels.map: Separate the event from your interpretation

context.description: During a project meeting, a colleague says, “I completed the project,” without naming the people who worked on it. I judge the comment as unfair and wonder whether fair credit matters to me. That is a possible value to examine, not proof of the colleague’s motive. I may not know who was asked to present or what others said earlier. Other examples and counterexamples can change the interpretation.

practice.instructions: Describe one event without naming the other person. Record the behavior you observed, the quality you assigned, and a value the reaction might point to. Add other examples and counterexamples before you treat the value as an explanation. Leave unknowns blank. This reflection does not diagnose another person or promise a therapeutic result.
practice.behavior: What specific behavior did you observe?
practice.quality: What quality did you assign to that behavior?
practice.value: What value might your reaction point to?
practice.examples: What other examples fit this interpretation?
practice.counterexamples: What counterexamples or missing facts weaken it?
practice.next: What fact or next action will you check before acting?
